dedupe_keys.name: uk region seir d modelling of interventions based on local hospital demand and capacity during covid 19

description: This case study develops an approach to timing epidemic interventions that is based on the demand and capacity of the local health services that must cope day to day, not on theoretical optimality. The authors, from the University of Sussex and Brighton and Sussex Medical School, published it as a preprint and later in PLOS ONE. They calibrate a susceptible, exposed, infectious, recovered and died (SEIR-D) model with data from a region of the UK to infer epidemic parameters, then forecast scenarios to see how the timing, severity and release conditions of interventions keep hospital demand below a given maximum capacity. Coverage is one UK region during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic. The preprint and the journal article are free and available online. Caveats: the model is compartmental and regional, capacity limits are assumed inputs, and case data during the pandemic were imperfect. The study shows how local authorities could use hospital capacity as the trigger for intervening and releasing measures. Simulation uses: an example of linking epidemic scenarios to hospital capacity planning for emergency response. Related records: the NHS capacity interventions study (case_study-nhs-england-covid19-hospital-capacity-interventions) and CHIME (model-chime) address the same question.
